**Comprehension (Q. 76 - 80):** Once a revered ritual, letter writing has steadily (1) ____ into a relic of bygone eras, displaced by the relentless immediacy of digital communication. There was a time when a single envelope, ink- smudged and weatherworn, (2) ____ profound intimacies across continents, preserving sentiments too sacred to entrust to fleeting conversations. Today's sterile texts and hastily composed emails seldom replicate the tactility that imbued handwritten letters with gravitas; every flourish, every hesitant stroke, bore the (3) vestiges of a soul laid bare. It is not merely nostalgia that compels some to cling to this endangered practice, but recognition that certain articulations of the heart (4) ____ better when filtered through the slowness of ink and parchment. Indeed, the act of penning a letter demands a kind of (5) deliberateness rare in an age characterized by impulsivity and ephemerality. Though the world races ever forward, perhaps in the margins of our modern lives, the art of letter-writing will preserve a fragile thread tethering us to a slower, richer past.
